claim: Histones are bound to cytosolic lipid droplets (LDs) under normal conditions.
source_text: We previously discovered histones bound to cytosolic lipid droplets (LDs); here we show that this forms a cellular antibacterial defense system. Sequestered on droplets under normal conditions

claim: In the presence of bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or lipoteichoic acid (LTA), histones are released from lipid droplets.

claim: Released histones kill bacteria efficiently in vitro.

claim: Embryos with droplet-bound histones displayed more than a fourfold survival advantage when challenged with four different bacterial species.

claim: This intracellular antibacterial defense system may function in adult flies.

claim: This intracellular antibacterial defense system potentially functions in mice.
